headline: High: shared filesystem and broad network/tooling in nullclaw create default data-leakage and cascading-error risks when paired with argo-workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Argo Workflows can expose artifacts/parameters, and nullclaw can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers/shell. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if argo outputs are surfaced into nullclaw’s file or message channels. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF argo-workflows outputs are copied into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or another watched file path
IF nullclaw parses workflow artifacts or web content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of workflow artifacts into nullclaw workspace
Require explicit human review before nullclaw acts on argo outputs
Tag argo-generated files as untrusted in the workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between workflow outputs and agent inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo Workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while nullclaw reads/writes workspace files, handles secrets, and has broad network egress. If shared data lands in nullclaw’s workspace, its default ability to transmit context or secrets creates a realistic exfiltration path. The blast radius includes tokens and private keys, so this is high.
conditions: IF artifacts or parameters contain secrets, credentials, or regulated data
IF those files are accessible under ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ or another shared path
IF nullclaw sends workspace contents to external APIs or webhooks
mitigations: Keep argo artifacts in a separate non-shared directory
Remove secrets from workflow parameters and artifacts
Restrict nullclaw network egress to approved destinations only
Rotate any credentials that may already have been written to shared files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo Workflows can operate on artifacts and parameters, while nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other. Because nullclaw explicitly supports multiple instances and shared durable memory, the conflict risk is not hypothetical.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or workspace directory
IF argo-workflows materializes outputs into files that nullclaw edits or commits
IF git state is shared without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes to the repo
Use file locks around shared mutable paths
Review and reconcile git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo Workflows can generate artifacts and parameters that nullclaw can read, browse, and act on with shell and network tools. If nullclaw treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions, including web requests or file changes. The pair lacks a verification boundary, so the default interaction is unsafe.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes argo outputs without an independent verification step
IF those outputs drive shell commands, web requests, or file writes
IF workflow artifacts contain incorrect or adversarial content
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before nullclaw acts on argo outputs
Require schema validation for workflow artifacts
Limit nullclaw to read-only review of argo results
Log and diff all downstream actions against source artifacts
requires-engineering: implement typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Argo Workflows is documented as a workflow engine with artifacts and parameters, while nullclaw handles workspace files, audit logs, and many secret classes. If regulated data is placed into shared workflow outputs, retention and residency controls can diverge across the pair. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in argo artifacts or parameters
IF nullclaw retains workspace files or audit logs longer than the workflow policy
IF the deployment subjects the same data class to different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify data before placing it in workflow artifacts
Align retention settings for workflow outputs and agent logs
Purge shared workspace files after each run
Review residency and DPA requirements for any regulated data
requires-engineering: unify retention policy enforcement
